title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
grouping: Three zones left to right. Left: training-data sources as beige rounded boxes - a large 'π dataset' box of cut-out robot pictures above two smaller boxes 'Internet pre-training' (globe and document icons) and 'OXE' (a globe with coloured stripes) - gathered by a tall right square bracket whose arrow points into the model. Middle: the model as two backbone bars - 'pre-trained VLM' and 'action expert' - each laid across a row of token columns; the action expert's columns sit in a beige panel. Right: a mirrored left square bracket fans out to three stacked beige boxes, each a robot photo with its embodiment name ('14 DoF Bimanual Manipulators', '18 DoF Mobile Manipulators', '7 and 8 DoF Single Arm Manipulators').
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles, all text in a monospace typewriter face. VLM token columns are steel-teal rounded columns with white pill tokens above and below a long white rounded bar ('pre-trained VLM' with grey 'SigLIP (400M) + Gemma (2.6B)'); three teal 'ViT' trapezoids stand on three camera photos (one base view, two wrist views), and the fourth column takes the quoted command '"fold shirt"'. Action-expert columns are pale green with green-outlined pills; inputs q_t and 'noise' enter from below; dashed loop arrows inside each action column show repeated refinement, and outputs a_t, a_t+1, ..., a_t+H sit in a curly brace at the top.
proposed_highlight: Colour separates the two parts of the proposed model (teal VLM, green action expert) and parameter counts in grey under each name state their sizes; the data and robot zones on the sides are beige, so the model reads as the centre between them.
lesson: Bracket the many training-data sources into the model on the left and fan the model out with a mirrored bracket to the robot embodiments it controls on the right, so the figure reads as many datasets -> one policy -> many robots.
notes: Venue not verified (remembered as RSS 2025; Semantic Scholar not queried for this title because of rate limits): venue written as arXiv, year = arXiv preprint year (2410.24164). Photos and robot pictures are embedded rasters.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: training 'other' = flow matching for the action expert; built on a PaliGemma-style VLM (SigLIP + Gemma); the VLM and action expert act as two weight sets in one transformer

core.what: one model of two token-column groups, blue VLM columns for images and the instruction and green action-expert columns for state and noisy actions, each group threaded by one long white bar, flanked by a bracketed data stack on the left and a bracketed embodiment stack on the right

relations.form: a long white 'pre-trained VLM' bar crosses all four blue token columns and a white 'action expert' bar crosses the green columns, sitting end to end on one line so the two experts read as one transformer
inputs enter each column from below: three camera photos through ViT trapezoids, the quoted 'fold shirt' instruction, the state q_t, and 'noise' under the action-expert panel
inside a tan panel the action-expert columns carry dashed loop arrows from bottom to top, the flow-matching refinement, emitting the action chunk a_t, a_t+1, ..., a_t+H above

left to right: training data stack (pi dataset, Internet pre-training, OXE) gathered by a bracket into the model, then a bracket out to three target-robot boxes (14 DoF bimanual, 18 DoF mobile, 7 and 8 DoF single arm)
data are drawn as data: real robot photos in the dataset and embodiment boxes, real camera frames of a shirt under the ViTs, a globe glyph for OXE

channels.colour: blue = VLM (vision-language) tokens and ViTs, green = action-expert tokens, tan = data/embodiment boxes and the action-expert's surrounding panel (tan carries two roles)
channels.shape: rounded columns with pills = token groups, long white bar = transformer layers, trapezoid = ViT, brackets = grouping of datasets and of robots
channels.line: solid arrows = inputs and outputs; dashed looped arrows = iterative denoising inside the action expert
channels.frame: tan rounded boxes = one dataset or robot type; tan panel = the action expert's denoising scope

quality.strengths: The two-expert design is visible as geometry: token columns of two colours share one bar line, the action expert is visibly smaller, and the denoising loop is drawn as dashed loops on its own columns; inputs and embodiments are real photos so the cross-embodiment claim is concrete.
quality.weaknesses: Tan fills both the data/robot boxes and the action-expert panel; the large brackets to the side stacks connect them to the whole model by one line each, so which data trains which part is not shown; the side stacks take about half of the width.

insights.structure: Three columns: a left stack of tan data boxes (pi dataset, Internet pre-training, OXE) gathered by a bracket, a center model where blue VLM token columns and green action-expert token columns are threaded by one long white bar per expert, and a right stack of three tan embodiment boxes (14/18/7-8 DoF) gathered by a bracket.
insights.data: Inputs sit under the model: three real camera frames feed ViT trapezoids, the instruction appears as the quoted string "fold shirt", q_t and noise arrive as bare labels with arrows, and the output action chunk a_t ... a_t+H is a bracketed token row on top.
insights.emphasis: Color splits the two experts (blue = pre-trained VLM, green = action expert with a tan backing panel), and the dashed looping arrows inside the green panel signal iterative flow-matching denoising of the action tokens.
insights.flow: Left-to-right at the top level (data -> model -> robots), but bottom-to-top inside the model (images/text/noise up through token columns to actions).
insights.avoid: The left data panel and right robot panel connect only through brackets, so it is unclear whether they are inputs/outputs or just context; the parameter counts in grey compete with the expert names.

arrangement.units: one model composition flanked by two bracketed side stacks (training data on the left, target embodiments on the right) of tan rounded boxes; the model has two colored token-column groups (blue VLM, green action expert inside a tan panel)
arrangement.inputs_as: real camera photos under ViT trapezoids plus a quoted instruction and noise/state labels
arrangement.shared: one long white bar across each expert's token columns shows shared attention layers
